results.title: Art’s New Season: Retrospectives and Resistance - The New York Times
results.content: Holland Cotter’s highlights include a panoptic view of Roy Lichtenstein, storytelling surprises of the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art, and activism from Colombia to South Asia to New York. But both here and nationally it will be exhibitions touching on the now under-censure subject of social justice that promises to give the season a sense of grit and purpose. The big popular draw in New York will surely be “Roy Lichtenstein: Like New,” a career retrospective of the pioneering and prolific Pop artist at the Whitney Museum of American Art (opening Oct. 11). One of the most influential of the 20th-century sculptors, the Romanian-born Constantin Brancusi spent much of his long career in Paris, where his studio functioned as both a crucible for new work and a self-dedicated museum during and after his life. So it’s good to see at the Metropolitan Museum of Art stretching that view with “Krasner and Pollock: Past Continuous” (Oct. 4-Jan. 31, 2027).

results.title: Announcement on The Met’s Spring 2027 Costume Institute Exhibition - The Metropolitan Museum of Art
results.content: (New York, August 31, 2026)—The Metropolitan Museum of Art and John Galliano together announced today that the exhibition *John Galliano: Horizons,* previously scheduled to open in May 2027, will not proceed as planned. **Statement from Max Hollein, Director and CEO of The Metropolitan Museum of Art:** “Following thoughtful discussions with John Galliano, we have together decided not to proceed with the exhibition.". **John Galliano** stated: "I am profoundly grateful to The Metropolitan Museum of Art, and particularly to Max Hollein, Andrew Bolton and Anna Wintour, for the extraordinary honour of proposing an exhibition devoted to my work.
